translations.text: And it came to pass in the days when the judges judged that there was a famine in the land. And a man went from Bethlehem of Judea to sojourn in the country of Moab, he and his wife and his two sons.

And his name was Elimelech, and the name of his wife was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites from Bethlehem of Judea. And they went to the land of Moab and lived there.
And Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left, she and her two sons.
And her sons took Moabite wives for themselves; the name of the one was Orpah and the name of the other was Ruth. And they lived there ten years.
And both of her sons, Mahlon and Chilion, died, and the woman was left alone, bereft of her husband and of her two sons.

And the woman arose with both her daughters-in-law, and they returned from the land of Moab to the country of Judea, for they had heard in the land of Moab that the Lord had visited his people to give them produce.
And she went out from that land, and her two daughters-in-law with her, and they set out on the road to return to the land of Judea.
And Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law: "Go, return each to your father's house, and may the Lord deal mercifully with you, as you have dealt with the dead and with me.
And may the Lord repay you for this kindness, and may you find rest in the house of your husband." And she kissed them and was parting from them. And they lifted up their voices and wept.
And they said to her: "Not so, but we will come with you to your people."
And Naomi said to them: "Turn back, my daughters, and go. Why would you come with me? Are there still sons in my womb from now on, that they might become husbands to you?
But now go, my daughters, for I have grown old and am no longer able to have a husband. Even if I were to tell you that I am still able, and I were joined to a husband and bore sons,

would you wait for them until they grew up, and would they keep you from having husbands? Not so, my daughters, for it has become more bitter for me than for you, for the hand of the Lord has gone out against me."
And they lifted up their voices and wept yet again. And Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and went back to her people, but Ruth clung to her and followed her.
And Naomi said to Ruth: "See, your companion has gone back to her people and to her gods. Go back yourself with your companion!"

Ruth answered and said: "May it not befall me to do that, to leave you and turn back and go to my home. But wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you dwell, I too will dwell with you. Your people is my people, and your God is my God.
And where you die, I too will die, and there I will be buried. May the Lord do this to me and add more to it, for death alone shall part you and me."
And when she saw that Ruth was so determined to go with her, she stopped speaking to her about it.
And the two of them went on from there and came to Bethlehem. And when they reached Bethlehem, the whole city groaned over them and said: "Is this really Naomi?"
And she said to them: "Do not call me Naomi, but call me Bitterness, for the Mighty One has dealt bitterly with me.
For I went out full, and the Lord has brought me back empty. Why do you call me Naomi? The Lord has humbled me, and the Mighty One has done me harm!
So Naomi returned. She came back, and Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, came with her; they came from the land of Moab. They arrived in Bethlehem at the very beginning of the barley harvest.
And Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Let me go out to the field and glean ears of grain behind someone in whose eyes I may find favor." And Naomi said to her, "Go, my daughter."
So she went out, came to a field, and gleaned ears of grain in it behind the reapers. As it happened, she came to the part of the field that belonged to Boaz, who was of the family of Elimelech.
And behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the reapers, "The Lord be with you!" And they said to him, "The Lord bless you!"
And Boaz said to his servant who was in charge of the reapers, "Who is this young woman?"
The servant who was in charge of the reapers answered Boaz, "This is the Moabite woman who came from the land of Moab.
She said, 'Let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the reapers.' So she came, and she has been here from dawn until now, and she has not rested even a little in this field."
And Boaz said to Ruth, "I say to you, my daughter: do not go to glean in another field, and do not leave here, but stay here close to my maidservants.

Keep your eyes on this field where they are reaping, and follow them. Behold, I have ordered my servants not to say anything to you. And when you are thirsty, go to the vessels and drink from what my servants drink."
Then Ruth fell on her face and bowed down to him on the ground. And she said to Boaz, "Why is it that I have found favor in your eyes, so that you take notice of me? I am a foreigner."

Boaz answered her, "I have been told in full all that you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband: you left your father and your mother and the land of your birth, and came to a people you did not know before.
May the Lord repay you for what you have done, and may you receive a full reward from the Lord, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge."
And she said, "May I have found favor before you, my lord, for you have comforted me and spoken kindly to the heart of your maidservant, and from now on I will be like one of your maidservants."

And Boaz said to her, "At mealtime come here, eat some bread, and dip your bread in the vinegar." So Ruth sat down beside the reapers, and Boaz passed her some roasted grain and gave it to her, and she ate and was satisfied.
Then she got up to glean, and Boaz gave orders to his servants, saying that she should be allowed to glean even among the sheaves, and "Do not shame her;
rather, be sure to take care of her, give her some of your food, and leave it for her, so that she may eat and glean; and do not scold her."
So she gleaned in the field until evening, and she threshed out what she had gathered, and it came to about one measure of barley.
She picked it up and went into the town, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gathered. Ruth also took out and gave her what she had left over after she had eaten her fill.

And her mother-in-law said to her: "Where did you glean today, daughter, and where did you get all this? Blessed be the man who took notice of you!" And Ruth told her mother-in-law where she had gleaned, and told her the man's name: "The man I gleaned with today is called Boaz."

Naomi said to her daughter-in-law: "May that man be blessed by the Lord, for he has not given up his kindness to the living and to the dead." And Naomi said: "That man is close to us, and he is also our kinsman."
Ruth said to her mother-in-law: "He also said to me: 'Stay with my maidservants until they have finished the whole harvest, all that is mine.'"
And Naomi said to Ruth, her daughter-in-law: "It is good, daughter, that you went out with his maidservants and did not go to someone else's field."
And Ruth stayed with Boaz's maidservants, gleaning for herself, until they had finished the barley harvest. And Ruth went home and lived with her mother-in-law.
"Daughter, should I not now seek rest for you, so that it may go well with you?
"Now Boaz, whose maidservants you were with, is someone we know, and tonight he is gathering barley on his threshing floor.
"So wash and anoint yourself, put on your clothes, and go up to his threshing floor. But do not let the man see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
"And when he lies down, take note of the place where he lies. Then go close to him and lie down at his feet, and he will tell you what you should do."
Ruth said to her mother-in-law: "I will do everything you have told me."
And she went up to his threshing floor and did just as her mother-in-law had instructed her.
And Boaz ate and drank, and his heart was merry, and he went and lay down [?] by the heap of his [?]. And Ruth came to him secretly and lay down close to him, at his feet.
And at midnight the man woke up and was startled, and he trembled, because a woman was lying at his feet.
Boaz said to her: "Who are you?" And she said to him: "I am Ruth, your maidservant. Spread your garment over your maidservant, for you are my kinsman."
Boaz said to her: "May you be blessed by the Lord, daughter, for this last kindness you have shown is greater than the first, since you did not go after young men, whether poor or rich.
"And now do not be afraid! [?] I will do for you everything you have told me, for all the kin of my people know that you are a woman of worth.
"Now it is true that I am a kinsman, but there is another kinsman closer than I am.

"Stay here tonight, and in the morning, if he will take you as his kin, let him take you. But if he does not want to take you as kin, I will take you, as the Lord lives!" And she lay there until dawn.
And she slept at his feet until morning. And she got up early, before anyone could recognize his neighbour, and Boaz said: "Let no one know that a woman came to this threshing floor."

And Boaz said: "Hold out to me here the garment you are wearing, and spread it open." And she held it out to him. And he measured out six measures of barley for her and laid it on her, and he went into the city.
And Ruth went in to her mother-in-law. And she said to her: "How did it go, daughter?" And she told her everything the man had done for her.
And she said to her: "He gave me these six measures of barley, and he said to me: 'Do not go to your mother-in-law empty-handed.'"
And she said to her: "Sit still, daughter, until you understand how the matter will not fall to the ground, for the man will not keep silent until he has settled the matter this very day."
[?] ... And he turned him aside, and he sat down there.
And Boaz brought ten men from the elders of the city and said to them: "Sit down!" And they sat down.
And Boaz said to the kinsman: "The portion of land of my brother Elimelech is to be given to Naomi, who has come from the land of Moab.

And I said: 'I will make it known to your ears.'" And he said to him: "Buy it in the presence of these who are sitting here, and in the presence of the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, redeem it; if you will not redeem it, tell me, so that I may know, for there is no other kinsman besides you, and after you I come." And he said: "I will; I will redeem it."

And Boaz said: "On the day when the land is bought from the hand of Naomi and from Ruth the Moabite, the wife of her son, whose husband died, buy the inheritance for yourself and take her also for yourself, so that through her you may raise up an heir for the dead man on his inheritance."
The kinsman said: "I cannot redeem it for myself, or I may ruin my own inheritance. You redeem it in place of my right to the inheritance, for I am not able to redeem it."

And this was formerly the custom in Israel concerning redemption and concerning exchange, so that every matter might be confirmed: a man would take off his sandal and give it to his neighbour who was redeeming his right of redemption. And this was the attestation in Israel.
And the kinsman said to Boaz: "Take my right of redemption for yourself!" And he took off his sandal and gave it to him.
Boaz said to the elders and to all the people: "You are witnesses today that I have bought all that belonged to Elimelech and to Mahlon from the hand of Naomi.

And Ruth the Moabite, the wife of Mahlon, I have acquired for myself as a wife, to raise up the name of the dead man on his inheritance. And the name of the dead man shall not be blotted out from among his brothers or from the tribes of his place. You are witnesses today."

And all the people who were sitting at the gates answered and said: "We are witnesses!" And the elders said to him: "May the Lord make your wife, who is entering your house, like Rachel and like Leah, who both built up the house of Israel; and may they bring about strength in Ephrathah and a name to be called in Bethlehem.
And may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, of your kindred; and may the Lord give you offspring by this maidservant of yours."
And Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. And he went in to her, and the Lord granted her conception, and she bore a son.
And the women spoke to Naomi and said to her: "Blessed is the Lord, who has secured redemption for you today, so that your name may be called in Israel.
And he shall be to you a restorer of the soul and a nourisher of your old age, for your daughter-in-law has borne a son, who is better to you than seven sons."
And Naomi took the child and laid him in her bosom and became his nurse.
And the neighbouring women gave him a name and said: "A son has been born to Naomi." And they called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
And these are the generations of Perez: Perez begot Hezron,
Hezron begot Ram, Ram begot Amminadab,
Amminadab begot Nahshon, Nahshon begot Salmon,
Salmon begot Boaz, Boaz begot Obed.
And Obed begot Jesse, and Jesse begot King David, the great, the chosen.
